## Ticket proposals
- **Close the gaps tests/test_package.py leaves in its own promises** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-079]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: The guard test is what keeps the SPD-065 package safe as it changes, and three of its checks are narrower than the sentences they are written to enforce. It collects bound names from Name stores and parameters only, so a nested def, a class statement, an except ... as, a match capture or a function-level import ... as can bind a module alias and the test still passes. Its cycle check reads only alias.name written outside a function body, so an import-time read reached through the module's own function is invisible. Its patch-target check tracks only variables assigned directly from load_spud_module(), so a patch through an alias of that object passes. Nothing in the tree today trips any of them, so this is protection for the next change, not a fix.
  Evidence: In scratch copies of the SPD-065 branch, each of these passes the guard test (python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -p test_package.py): a nested def walk() inside a function of shell/analyse; except Exception as syntax inside a function of shell/globbing; def _probe(): return walk.ShellWalk with _PROBE = _probe() at the top of shell/analyse; and a test doing m = spud; mock.patch.object(m, 'now', ...). The nine damage cases the test does promise to catch all fail as they should. The fix is small: build the binding set with symtable, which sees every binding form, and treat a top-level call of a module's own function as an import-time read. Cherie's review, docs/spikes/spd-065/review.md, finding 1.
